hero.title_html:
Krewire v0.1.0 is Here.
The Modular Go Ecosystem for 8 Workloads.
hero.lead: The official release launchpad for the Krewire open-source ecosystem. A unified, modular Go foundation engineered with single monorepo architecture, one declarative config (krewire.yaml), and one developer CLI (kiw) — crafted in Indonesia for software engineers and autonomous AI agents worldwide.
hero.meta: Go 1.27.1+ · Single Monorepo · 8 Unified Workloads · Spec-Driven Testing

releases.title: Krewire Ecosystem v0.1.0 Launch
releases.subtitle: The foundational milestone release delivering single monorepo architecture, the kiw devtool, strictly typed manifests, and 8 unified workload shapes.
releases.f1_desc: Consolidated under github.com/krewire/krewire. Eliminates cross-module dependency fragmentation, guarantees atomic Git commits, and powers seamless Go workspaces (go.work).
releases.f2_desc: A single binary driving the software lifecycle: kiw new, kiw dev, kiw build, kiw serve, kiw worker, kiw deploy, and kiw boost.
releases.f3_desc: Strictly typed, declarative project manifests eliminating arbitrary configuration drift across all 8 supported workloads.
releases.f4_desc: Single-purpose packages under packages/* (kern, web, ui, cli, db, config, validation, fs, worker). Compose only what you need without inheriting a monolithic framework.
releases.f5_desc: First-class integration for autonomous AI developer agents (templates/boost) with formal KWF-* specifications, automated audits, and regression tests.
releases.f6_desc: Standalone Markdown book & docs compiler powering the book kind with AST transformations, live reloads, and offline assets embedding.

workloads.title: 8 Workload Kinds Behind One Engine
workloads.subtitle: Krewire adapts to your project shape. An explicit project.kind in krewire.yaml determines the build, runtime, and deployment lifecycle.
workloads.w_app_desc: Fullstack web applications with reactive server rendering, context pipelines, and DI containers.
workloads.w_cli_desc: Ergonomic terminal tools, subcommands, and flags powered by the lightweight TUI library.
workloads.w_site_desc: High-speed static websites, marketing portals, and blogs with scoped CSS and the .kiw DSL.
workloads.w_book_desc: Technical documentation and digital books compiled with the standalone mdbind engine.
workloads.w_worker_desc: Background task processors, concurrent runners, async queues, and scheduled cron jobs.
workloads.w_service_desc: High-throughput microservices, headless daemons, and low-latency JSON/gRPC APIs.
workloads.w_infra_desc: Zero-downtime raw VM runners, SSH automation, automated TLS provisioning, and systemd manifests.
workloads.w_runtime_desc: Compile Go into WebAssembly with virtual DOM diffing, reactive interactive islands, and partial client hydration.

navigator.title: 5 Core Repositories & Where to Start
navigator.subtitle: Match your skills and background to the right repository, bootstrap your local environment, and dive straight into active issues.
navigator.one_line_desc_html: Automatically clones all ecosystem repositories, creates your go.work workspace, builds the kiw devtool, and validates compatibility contracts:
navigator.match_krewire: If you enjoy: Modular Go libraries (packages/*), CLI devtool (tools/kiw), fullstack runtimes, background queues, and AI agent templates (templates/boost).
navigator.match_mdbind: If you enjoy: Lightning-fast static documentation builders, Markdown AST transformations, instant live reload, search indexing, and syntax highlighters.
navigator.match_krewire_com: If you enjoy: High-fidelity web design, interactive documentation, component-driven layouts, and dogfooding the .kiw DSL in production.
navigator.match_github_io: If you enjoy: Community engagement, release showcases, localization (i18n), accessible UI components, and contributor onboarding portals.
navigator.match_internal: If you enjoy: Architectural Decision Records (ADRs), Spec-Driven Development (KWF-*), long-term roadmaps, and ecosystem governance.

roadmap.title: Ecosystem Evolution & Release Ladder
roadmap.subtitle: Our progressive open core release roadmap across the four-rung ladder: free → pro → team → enterprise.
roadmap.v1_desc: Single monorepo, 8 workload kinds, unified kiw CLI, mdbind compiler, and Spec-Driven Testing contracts.
roadmap.v2_desc: Advanced worker distributed schedulers, enterprise RBAC/Auth wrappers, multi-cloud infra targets, and telemetry hooks.
roadmap.v3_desc: WASM client-side hydration, automatic canary deployments, and autonomous agent self-healing workflows.

pillars.title: Engineered for Autonomy, Built for Longevity
pillars.subtitle: Krewire is not just another web framework. It is an open architectural collective solving software fragmentation, ballooning cloud costs, and developer fatigue.
pillars.p1_desc: Built from ground up to support self-healing, self-building pipelines, and native orchestration by autonomous AI agents (Boost).
pillars.p2_desc: Zero hand-waving. Every architectural boundary begins with formal specifications (KWF-*) and clear contract interfaces before implementation.
pillars.p3_desc: Radical resource efficiency. Go standard-library minimalism designed to operate smoothly on $5 VPS nodes up to hyperscale infrastructure.
pillars.p4_desc: Specialized AI agents (Boost) act as first-class team members — auditing security, catching regressions, and helping contributors iterate faster.

benefits.title: Lifetime Access to Krewire's Paid Ecosystem
benefits.subtitle: Genuine appreciation for true builders. By joining and actively contributing to the Krewire open source collective, you earn lifetime access to our upcoming commercial sub-products and premium ecosystem tools.
benefits.b1_desc: Receive free lifetime licenses for upcoming commercial Krewire products — including managed cloud orchestration tools, enterprise modules, and premium services.
benefits.b1_i1: Free lifetime access to all paid Krewire commercial sub-products
benefits.b1_i2: Priority early-access releases and exclusive roadmap previews
benefits.b1_i3: Direct private collaboration channels with core maintainers
benefits.b2_desc: This privilege is a two-way commitment. Your access remains active as long as you regularly contribute and help nurture the ecosystem's growth.
benefits.b2_i1: Submit PRs for new features, bugfixes, or kernel optimizations
benefits.b2_i2: Review open PRs and stress-test high-concurrency scenarios
benefits.b2_i3: Author KWF architecture specifications or comprehensive docs
benefits.b3_desc: To protect community fairness and true meritocracy, commercial access licenses may be revoked at any time if a contributor becomes inactive or dormant over an extended period.
benefits.b3_i1: Contributor activity and commits are periodically audited
benefits.b3_i2: Prolonged inactivity or dormancy leads to license deactivation
benefits.b3_i3: Access privileges can be promptly reinstated upon resumed contribution
benefits.policy_text: We believe those who lay the foundation should share in its fruits. Commercial access is free for all active contributors, provided ongoing dedication to the collective is consistently maintained.

standards.title: The Krewire Way: 3 Quality Gates
standards.subtitle: To keep the codebase reliable, predictable, and production-ready, every pull request passes through three automated gates.
standards.gate1_desc: Zero lint errors and idiomatic Go formatting. Code must adhere strictly to Go standard conventions.
standards.gate2_desc: Every commit is verified with race condition detection and comprehensive unit & integration tests.
standards.gate3_desc: Changes must link to a valid Spec or Issue, following Conventional Commits format.

guild.title: Collaborating with AI Boost
guild.lead: Krewire pioneers the collaboration between human maintainers and autonomous AI agents. Our AI Boost framework operates with strict verification standards:
guild.item1_html: Automated Architecture Audits: AI agents check PRs against KWF-* specifications.
guild.item2_html: Continuous Regression Hunting: Agents synthesize edge cases and race condition checks.
guild.item3_html: Transparent Pair Programming: AI agents explain architectural decisions openly in discussions and PR comments.
guild.item4_html: Human Governance: Ultimate merging authority always remains in the hands of human collective maintainers.
guild.planner_desc: Translates feature ideas into formal specs and architectural blueprints.
guild.builder_desc: Generates clean Go implementations adhering to idiomatic patterns.
guild.auditor_desc: Validates concurrency, zero data races, and performance benchmarks.
